title: Combustion and fuels; Stereoisomerism (E/Z and optical)
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for OCR A-level (A) Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EN11#t1 term and clue written for the game; EN11#t2 term and clue written for the game; EN11#t4 term and clue written for the game; EN11#t3 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EN11#N.3, OR05#N.4a, EN11#N.5, OR05#N.5, EN11#N.8, OR05#N.8, EN11#N.15, OR05#N.14c.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Complete combustion
items.clue: Burning in plenty of O₂, so that all C ends as CO₂ and all H as H₂O.

items.label: Carbon monoxide
items.clue: Colourless, odourless, toxic gas formed when a fuel burns in limited oxygen.

items.label: Haemoglobin
items.clue: Substance in red blood cells that binds CO far more strongly than it binds O₂.

items.label: Soot
items.clue: Solid C from burning in limited oxygen; glowing particles of it make a flame yellow.

questions.stem: When the equation for the complete combustion of octane, C₈H₁₈, is balanced with a coefficient of 2 for octane, what is the coefficient of O₂?
questions.explanation: 2C₈H₁₈ forms 16CO₂ and 18H₂O, which contain 16 × 2 + 18 = 50 O atoms. Each O₂ supplies two O atoms, so 25 O₂ are needed.

questions.stem: In one stereoisomer of 2-chlorobut-2-ene, CH₃CCl=CHCH₃, the Cl atom and the H atom are on the same side of the C=C. Which is correct?

options.text: It is Z, because the Cl atom and the H atom are on the same side.
It is E, because the priority groups, Cl and CH₃, are on opposite sides.
It is Z, because the two CH₃ groups are on the same side.
It has no E/Z isomers, because one of its C=C carbons carries a CH₃ group.

questions.explanation: C2: Cl outranks CH₃. C3: CH₃ outranks H. Cl is on the H side, so it is opposite the CH₃ on C3: E.

questions.stem: What amount of oxygen, O₂, is needed to burn 0.500 mol of propan-1-ol, C₃H₇OH, completely?
questions.explanation: C₃H₇OH + 4½O₂ → 3CO₂ + 4H₂O. The products contain 10 O atoms; the alcohol supplies 1, so O₂ supplies 9: 4½ O₂ per mole. 0.500 × 4.5 = 2.25 mol.

questions.stem: Which compound can exist as E and Z stereoisomers about its C=C bond?
questions.explanation: Each C=C carbon carries an H and a C₂H₅. Rotation is blocked, so the two arrangements are different compounds.

questions.stem: Which equation represents an incomplete combustion of ethanol?
questions.explanation: In very limited O₂ the carbon is deposited as soot while the hydrogen still forms water. 3 O atoms in the products: 1 from ethanol, 2 from O₂.

questions.stem: Which carbon atom in 3-methylhexane, CH₃CH₂CH(CH₃)CH₂CH₂CH₃, is a chiral centre?

options.text: None, as every group on C3 starts with a carbon atom.

questions.explanation: C3 carries H, CH₃, C₂H₅ and CH₂CH₂CH₃: four different groups.

questions.stem: After cooking outdoors, campers carry a still-glowing charcoal barbecue into their closed tent for warmth. Charcoal is almost pure carbon. Why is this deadly, even though there is no flame?

options.text: The charcoal burns to extra carbon dioxide, C + O₂ → CO₂, which binds to haemoglobin in place of oxygen.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, an acidic gas that damages the lungs.
With limited oxygen, carbon burns to carbon monoxide, 2C + O₂ → 2CO, which binds to haemoglobin.
The charcoal uses up all of the oxygen in the tent, and this lack of oxygen suffocates the campers.

questions.stem: Butan-2-ol, CH₃CH(OH)CH₂CH₃, exists as two stereoisomers with identical boiling points. Which explains why there are two?

options.text: Rotation about the C2–C3 bond is restricted, so the molecule has E and Z isomers.
C2 has four different groups, so the molecule cannot be superimposed on its mirror image.
The –OH group can be on C1 or on C2 of the chain, so there are two position isomers of it.
Every molecule has a mirror image, so every organic compound exists as two stereoisomers.

questions.explanation: C2 carries H, OH, CH₃ and C₂H₅: a chiral centre. The two stereoisomers are enantiomers.
